narrative:
The model determined that you have a 91.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the law school sets a high bar for admission and this probability is so high, your application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by your academic performance during law school. Your first-year and third-year class rankings were the two strongest factors pushing the prediction toward failure. Both placed you in the bottom decile of your class—far below the average of accepted students, who typically ranked around the middle of their class in those years. These unusually low rankings strongly signaled to the model that you would struggle with the bar exam.

Your LSAT score was the third most important factor, but it worked in the opposite direction. At 37, it sits almost exactly at the average of students who were accepted, which slightly helped your chances. Unfortunately, this positive influence was not nearly enough to offset the much larger negative impact of your class rankings.

The model did not consider your gender or race in any way. Your family income, undergraduate GPA, and plan to attend full-time were also far less influential.

To improve your prospects, you should focus on strengthening your academic performance or seek additional bar exam preparation resources before reapplying. Raising your class standing in future years or demonstrating significant improvement could substantially change how a similar model evaluates your application next time. (218 words)
prompt:
A machine learning model predicted that a student will FAIL the bar exam and therefore their application for university admission was REJECTED. Your goal is to generate an explanatory narrative based on the information provided (1-5), explaining why the law school application was denied for this student.

1. DATASET INFORMATION
The dataset contains information on students who took the bar exam.

The target variable is whether the student passed the bar exam on the first try (0 = passed, 1 = failed).

Protected attributes gender and race were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward "will fail" (bar exam failure), negative toward "will pass" (bar exam success). Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. STUDENT PROFILE 
You are writing a narrative tailored to this specific person who is rejected law school admission. 
Feature values (with comparisons to students who were accepted where available - showing distribution or average among students who were accepted):

- decile3 = 1.00 (the decile to which the student belongs in the school given his grades in Year 3.) - average: 5.79

- gender = male (the gender of the student.)

- Predicted probability of failure: 91.9%

Feature  SHAP_Value

Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
1) The model's predicted probability of bar exam failure and what this means for the student.
